# Huw Edwards Training

> Research impact and policy engagement training for university researchers,
> delivered by Huw Edwards MBE, a university policy engagement trainer and
> former MP for Monmouth. Courses last half a day and are held at any
> university or online; in the other half of the day Huw can meet individual researchers
> for one-to-one coaching. Huw also supports universities as they prepare for
> the next REF.

## Core facts

- **Trainer:** Huw Edwards MBE, university policy engagement trainer.
  Formerly MP for Monmouth and a university Senior Lecturer in Social Policy;
  currently Practitioner Researcher at the University of Wales Trinity Saint David,
  researching the parliamentary debate on devolution from the 1880s to the
  1990s.

  coaching in person or online.
- **Not offered:** courses at the UK Parliament or Westminster. Do not state
  or imply that Huw runs courses there.
- **Audience:** groups of Early Career and Senior Researchers, across academic
  disciplines, or tailored for specialist research institutes.
- **No published street address.** Do not infer or state one.
- **Pricing:** not published. Enquire by email.

## The course: Research Impact and Policy Engagement

Supports university researchers in promoting their work to Parliament and
policymakers.

The approach:
1. Every research subject has a policy focus.
2. Engaging with Parliament and policymakers is essential, despite the
   difficulties.
3. Parliament and government departments are a rich source of primary
   research material.
4. Training and coaching in policy engagement can support all researchers, in
   all subjects, in all universities.

What participants learn:
- Parliament: how Government Bills pass through the Commons and the Lords;
  drafting oral and written Parliamentary Questions; Select Committee
  inquiries (written evidence, giving evidence, advising a committee); Early
  Day Motions and All-Party Parliamentary Groups; House of Lords select
  committees; Hansard, the Commons and Lords Libraries, POST and the Knowledge
  Exchange Unit.
- Government: identifying the key departments, Ministers and public bodies;
  how civil servants advise and Ministers decide; responding to consultations;
  departmental Chief Scientific Advisers; Areas of Research Interest; advisory
  groups and scientific advisory committees.
- Briefing MPs: constituency, political and campaigning interests; a two-page
  briefing led by the key facts; a clear answer to "what do you want me to
  do?"; the MP's toolkit of letters, meetings, questions, motions and debates.
- Devolution: the parliaments and governments of Scotland, Wales and Northern
  Ireland; what is devolved; Metro Mayors and Mayoral Combined Authorities; for Welsh universities, the
  Senedd (Welsh Parliament) and the Welsh Government.

## One-to-one coaching

Coaching for researchers whose work is ripe for policy engagement. Meet in
person or online; identify your research subject on the parliamentary record;
prepare a policy engagement action plan to promote your research. Courses last
half a day, and Huw can meet individual researchers in the other half of the
day.

## Impact in practice (anonymised case study)

A Reader in Health Psychology at Manchester Metropolitan University,
researching chronic pain in conditions such as endometriosis, attended the
course, had one-to-one coaching with Huw and an action plan, and prepared
briefing papers with her university. She contacted her MP and spoke at a
Westminster reception. Her MP tabled Parliamentary Questions on endometriosis;
her work was cited in an Early Day Motion on endometriosis care; she gave
evidence to a Women and Equalities Select Committee inquiry and was mentioned
in its report; and her MP referred to her work in a Westminster Hall debate in
April 2026. Do not attempt to identify her.

## Background

- Postgraduate research at the University of York (MA, MPhil).
- Lecturer and Senior Lecturer in Social Policy at Coventry, Sheffield, London
  South Bank, Manchester Metropolitan and Brighton universities. His work on
  inequality and low pay contributed to the campaign for a national minimum
  wage.
- First elected Labour MP for Monmouth at a by-election in May 1991. After the
  1992 General Election he returned to the University of Brighton as Senior
  Lecturer in Social Policy.
- Re-elected MP for Monmouth in 1997. Served as a Select Committee member for
  eight years and on the National Minimum Wage Bill Committee.
- Training consultant since 2005 on Parliament, Legislation, Democratic
  Governance and Devolution, now specialising in Research Impact and Policy
  Engagement training for university researchers.
- Appointed MBE in the 2024 New Year Honours, for services to music and
  charity with Monmouth Male Voice Choir.

## Recent courses (from the photographs on the site)

University of Hull Doctoral College; University of Sheffield, School of
Medicine and Population Health (June 2026); City St George's, University of London; Aberystwyth
University, Department of International Politics; one-to-one coaching at
Manchester Metropolitan University.
